steps.content:
To my gray-cloaked partner,
Hail and well met.

The woman pens the opening lines of her letter in the light of the rising sun. Another trading day begins, the camp gradually filling with commotion, amid the sounds of cargo being unloaded, haggling, and crass arguments.
Yet there she sits at the heart of this bustling scene, basking in the sun, writing her letter with elegant composure.

steps.speaker: Local A
steps.content: Whoa, these folks must be new around here. Haven't seen a woman leading a caravan in ages... Really hopped up, aren't they? That woman must get some serious chops!

steps.speaker: Local B
steps.content: Shhh, shut it! Who gave you the nerve to run your mouth about their boss, eh? Don't say I didn't warn you. If they hear what you're saying, you can kiss that tongue of yours goodbye!
The two locals who regularly hang around the camp looking for gigs and freebies shuffle past, their eyes darting away from Vautour Bleu as if scalded. Yet she doesn't even bother to turn her head.

steps.speaker: Accountant
steps.content: Spices, all in Section A. Fuel's been loaded too... Huh, why aren't these numbers adding up?

steps.speaker: Accountant
steps.content: Ah, n-no, Boss, nothing! Rest assured! I'll make sure everything balances before we leave. Or you can take me as the penalty!

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: What good would you be to me? There's hardly enough meat on your bones to be worth anything.
When Vautour Bleu waves her hand dismissively, the accountant scurries away with the notebook, grateful for the reprieve after being caught making a mistake.

steps.speaker: Deputy Captain
steps.content: Hey, Eiss! Have you seen Lyman?

steps.speaker: Assistant
steps.content: Wha—no! Probably passed out somewhere. Stop bothering me, I've got to see Boss!
With that, the short teenager bounces urgently toward Vautour Bleu in her lounge chair, grinning as he gives a playful salute.

steps.speaker: Assistant
steps.content: Morning, Boss! Here to report the spend! And I've got a few things to run by you too, hehe!

steps.speaker: Assistant
steps.content: First of all, about yesterday's diner for the crew. I was gonna put it on our book, but Finn insisted it was all on him 'cause he's local here... Said we can pay him back double once we calculate the profits, so we didn't spend a single penny!

steps.speaker: Assistant
steps.content: Then, the raw materials for color-shifting ink were cheaper than last time, so we bought nine extra crates. Also got three pressing machines...

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Engraving machines.
The woman, sorting the envelopes in her hands, corrects him offhandedly.

steps.speaker: Assistant
steps.content: Understood! The engraving machines are grouped with the turquoise, blue amber, and other jewelry in Section D. We'll unload everything together at the next stop. Also, we've scheduled one day for resupply. We plan to depart tomorrow morning. Your approval?

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: It's settled, then.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Before we go, mail this letter for me, along with those gifts in the back seat.
The deep blue envelope bears her unique vulture wax seal. It's clearly fancy stuff meant to mail through the exclusive routes.

steps.speaker: Assistant
steps.content: Is this... a letter to DisCity? Holy Boss, you've got connections there too!
A slight smirk tugs at her lips as wisps of smoke drift up, veiling her enigmatic expression.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Connections? Hmph, just a former neighbor, nothing more.

To my gray-cloaked friend,
Greetings.

How have you been? I trust our mutual friends are settling in well after following you to DisCity.

Is our little homing dove still rushing about her delivery service? I suppose it's her way of finding herself—I can only hope you've lent her a hand along the way.

Has my freckled little brat learned to hold his tongue? It's better to behave in an unfamiliar place.

Talkative Juan always let his fists do the talking, but I'm sure you have more formidable figures there to keep him in check. And my dear Alba, I hope she rises to become the star she's always meant to be.

I've been trading along the western edge of WhiteSands lately. Seen many new things unknown to me during my more settled days.

I came across desert bandits. Boorish as ever, still hunting in packs and charging at their prey recklessly.

I also met a new tribe with rather unconventional artistic tastes. Trading with them required no words—quite the opposite, in fact. Absolute silence was their preferred language.

I've sent you a few souvenirs to adorn your office. I hope they'd spark interesting conversations with your guests.

I happened to pass by Désir the other day. That place where we spent those fleeting days together has vanished without a trace. Even that balcony we shared is gone with the wind, much like our memories.
...
You're halfway through the letter when Nightingale pushes open the door. She looks visibly startled by the collection of souvenirs covering your desk.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Chief, these sculptures...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: They're from Vautour Bleu. She said they'd make a great conversation starter.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Vautour Bleu, that trafficker at large? ...Understood.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Let me help you put these aside. They're taking up the entire desk.
As Nightingale clears your desk, you continue reading the letter, pausing occasionally for contemplation.

You allow yourself enough time to digest her words. You know Vautour Bleu isn't someone who'd waste time on trivial correspondence and strange gifts. She's an adversary who demands your full attention.
After that inconclusive confrontation in Désir, you know better than anyone that she's a born business mind. Meticulous and goal-oriented, she'll never make a losing deal.
Sure enough, after the pleasantries on the first page, Vautour Bleu reveals her true purpose on the next one.

...
I hate to admit it, but the crew of my new caravan is still quite green. They can't even keep track of their own people.

Last night, a man named Lyman went missing. We picked him up on the western route, battered and filthy as if just crawled out of a battlefield. He claimed he was robbed, but I could tell he was a deserter.

That happens a lot. Outside of DisCity, people fight disasters in their own way. Without equipage or Hypercubes like the FAC, even basic protection is a luxury.

In WhiteSands, lives are but dew.

Being the kind soul as I always am, I took him in and signed him to a year of service with all the necessary welfare. I also promised him a journey to the fabled paradise of DisCity afterward...

Dear, I can hear you snickering.

Désir is gone, but it's never truly lost.

Yet, he failed my trust. He fled with a good portion of our supplies. By the time this letter reaches you, he should be near the border. I trust you know what to do, right?
Hail and well met, my partner in justice. Yours, Vautour Bleu
Vautour Bleu's letter ends abruptly, very much in line with her style. She seldom speaks her mind directly, instead leaving others to decipher her true intentions through carefully placed hints.
If things turn out well, you owe her a favor. Otherwise, you've simply misinterpreted her meaning. So sophisticated.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Partner in justice... No such heroic character would stand by and watch someone suffer a merciless fate, even if it's some desperado on the run.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Using people as bargaining chips. Is this the trade you want, Vautour Bleu?
After careful consideration, you decide to accept this deal. After all, this is in DisCity, not Désir. Even if she is indeed plotting something, you're sure you can handle it.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Nightingale, notify the Border Bureau. We don't know what this man stole from the caravan yet, but he's unlikely to enter the city through legal channels. Conflicts is probably imminent.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Get our operatives ready. Let me know immediately once you locate him.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Chief, are you going there yourself?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: How else can I verify what we're dealing with if I don't? Don't worry. Vautour Bleu may be shrewd, but I don't make bad investments either.
Despite that, a shadow of doubt still lingers in your mind.
Vautour Bleu is a merchant for whom profit always comes first. So what drives her to reach out to you, share what she knows, and propose this deal? What does she really want?
You try to recall your time in Désir for clues, but the more you think, the less you figure out. Vautour Bleu's like a mirage in WhiteSands, ethereal, but potentially lethal if touched by.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Looks like we'll have to deal with it anyway, no matter how suspicious it is... Sitting here overthinking won't do any help.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You won't expect me to go easy on someone like you, would you? Business is war, Miss Merchant, and vice versa.
